\documentclass{article}
\begin{document}
Synthetic public demo with textbook many-body identities. It is not a
research manuscript.

For real $a\neq c$ let
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:summand}
F(z) = \frac{1}{(z-a)(z-c)} .
\end{equation}
The fermionic Matsubara sum is
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:fermion}
T\sum_n F(i\omega_n) = \frac{n_F(a)-n_F(c)}{a-c},
\end{equation}
and the bosonic one, valid when neither pole sits at $\nu_0=0$, is
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:boson}
T\sum_n F(i\nu_n) = -\frac{n_B(a)-n_B(c)}{a-c}.
\end{equation}
The free propagator
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:green}
G(i\omega) = \frac{1}{i\omega-\epsilon}
\end{equation}
has the high-frequency tail
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:tail}
G(i\omega) = \frac{1}{i\omega} + \frac{\epsilon}{(i\omega)^2} + O(\omega^{-3}).
\end{equation}
\end{document}
